effect.words: Which way does his nose take him?
effect.reply: Downwind of anything sweet. The wild trees down the mere shore drop their fruit early, so follow the fallers toward the water. And mind the camp along the shore, eh? There's wolves out there with no orchard of their own.

quests.title: The Fox at the Hen-Run
quests.summary: A fox is taking the hens that scratch round the Oakhurst pig yard. The soapworks hand who buys Oakhurst's fat wants it seen off.

offer.say: #greet#, #address#. Oakhurst sends us its pig fat for the soap, and the pig keeper says there's a fox at his hens, and the pigs just stand and watch it, the great lumps. Three birds this week. Find it in the scrub round the yard and see it off, eh? He can't leave the yard.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. A full net, that. Eggs from the hens that are left; the pig keeper sent them down with the fat. They'll lay better now they can sleep, eh?

objectives.label: Bring down the fox in the scrub round the Oakhurst pig yard.

quests.title: Bread to the Landing
quests.summary: Carry three of the Coldwater Bakehouse's loaves to the Coldwater Stores, for the boat crews on the Glasswater landing.

offer.say: #greet#. The boat crews on the Glasswater landing go out before my oven's warm, and they come back hungry as gulls. Three loaves over to the Stores: their hand takes the crews their bread with the catch cart. It's a short walk, eh?
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Full bellies on the water, and that's a fair catch. If you're ever going Southmeadow way, I might have a letter for you. Might, mind. #farewell#.

objectives.label: Give the three loaves to the Coldwater Stores hand, for the Glasswater landing.

quests.title: Wood for the Kettles
quests.summary: The Coldwater Boiling House kettles want firing all day. Bring firewood, and fat scraps if a hunt gave you any.

offer.say: #greet#, #address#. Soap, and the kettles want firing from dawn to dark. My woodpile's down to bark. Five bundles of firewood, eh? And if you've fat scraps from a hunt, I'll take two and thank you twice. Deep and dark, don't let my fires go out.
offer.accept: Five bundles, and fat if I find it.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Fair catch. Here's a cake of soap. Every wolf in Ridgemere could use one, but they won't buy soap from the lake, eh? Their loss.

objectives.label: Bring five bundles of firewood to the soap boiler.
Two fat scraps for the kettle, if a hunt gives you any (a badger gives two).

quests.title: The Pup Who Follows His Nose
quests.summary: The Meresend orchard's pup has followed his nose down the Upper Mere shore. Find him and bring him to the Glasswater Inn, where his mother will fetch him.

offer.say: #greet#. The Meresend orchard's pup has slipped off again, and his mother's out in the far rows; she sent word down with the apple cart. He can smell an apple a mile off. Down the shore by the wild trees, I'd wager. Fetch him back here to the inn, eh?
offer.handIn: Here's your pup, nose and all.
offer.thanks: There he is, nose first. #thanks#, #address#. Apples off the cart, the good ones. Still water finds its way back to the lake, the old ones say, and a pup finds his way back to the orchard. Mostly with help.

objectives.label: Find the orchard pup along the Upper Mere shore.
Bring him to the pot hand at the Glasswater Inn.
Bring down a bandit on the mere shore while you are there.

bonus.detail: brought down a bandit on the Upper Mere shore

quests.title: Straw for the Lambing Pens
quests.summary: Ewes lamb better on clean straw. Bring three bales to the Coldwater Looms for the Larkdowns pens, and walk the fold at dusk if you can.

offer.ask: Is the Looms short of wool?
offer.say: #greet#, #address#. The Looms buys the Larkdowns wool, and the shepherd sent word: his lambing pens are down to dust. Three bales of straw from the stores, brought here, and I'll cart them up with the empty sacks. And walk his fold at dusk, eh? A wolf the flock knows is one they don't run from.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. That's a full net for the flock. Clean straw, clean lambs, and clean wool for my loom come shearing. #farewell#.

objectives.label: Bring three bales of straw to the Looms, for the Larkdowns pens (every town store keeps straw).
Walk the Larkdowns fold at dusk, so the flock learns your scent.

quests.title: Wool on the Thorns
quests.summary: A ewe has strayed up the Larkdowns. Follow the wool she left on the thorns and say where the trail leads.

offer.say: #greet#, #address#. A Larkdowns ewe is off on the downs, and the shepherd can't leave the flock, so he sent down to the Looms for a good nose. She'll have left wool on every thorn she passed. Follow the tufts, pick up three, and come and tell me how far they lead, eh?
offer.handIn: I followed the wool to the end of it.
offer.thanks: That far, is it? I'll send word up, and he'll have her home before dark. #thanks#. Keep the wool; it's good fleece, and I'd know.

objectives.label: Follow the strayed ewe's wool on the downs round the shearing barn: pick up three tufts.

quests.title: Rope for the Drag
quests.summary: The Oakhaven carter's drag rope has gone to threads. A new coil from the Ridgemere ropewalk, carried along the Sound Road to the carter on the square. Rope is sold only in the city.

objectives.label: Give a coil of rope to the Oakhaven carter on the square.
On the road from the city, bring down a bandit at Alder Mere (before you hand over the rope).

rewards.text: Good bark, you. The drag's moving on your rope, mm? My grandmother would've called you sound wood.

bonus.detail: brought down a bandit on the Oakhaven road

quests.title: Venison for the Cut
quests.summary: The loggers at the Oakhaven cut live on bread. Bring down a roe deer in the Rainwood and carry the venison to the feller who asked.

offer.say: #greet#. The loggers eat bread and more bread, and a wolf can't fell cedar on bread, mm? A roe deer out of the Rainwood would feed the cut for days. They're shy. Come at them downwind, slow through the trees, and pray the Bright One keeps the wind steady.
offer.accept: A roe deer for the cut.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. The Bright One sent you, I'd say, though you'd say you walked. That's a favour I owe, and I keep count. Jerky from the last one, for your road. #farewell#.

objectives.label: Bring down a roe deer in the Rainwood by the cut.
Bring two cuts of the venison to the feller.

quests.title: A Quiet Head Before the Storm
quests.summary: A logger at the Oakhaven cut can't sleep before a storm. Bring him chamomile or valerian to quiet his head.

offer.ask: You look like you haven't slept.
offer.say: #greet#. There's a storm coming, I can feel it in my teeth, and I won't sleep a wink before it. Chamomile, if the meadows have any, or valerian from the stores. Anything to quiet the head, mm?
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Root and rain, I'll sleep now, even if the sky falls in. You've a good root in you, #address#.

objectives.label: Bring two sprigs of chamomile, or valerian, to the sleepless logger.
Once he has his herbs, be in Oakhaven when the storm breaks.

quests.title: Wood for the Pass House
quests.summary: The Pass House burns through its woodpile while the carters wait on the Pass Road. Look in at the Pass House, then give four bundles of firewood for the carters' stack to the Frosthollow carter on the square. Oats for the carters' pot are welcome too: give them before the wood.

objectives.label: Go into the Pass House and see how low the pile is.
Give four bundles of firewood to the Frosthollow carter on the square.
If you have them, two measures of oats for the carters' pot (give them before the last of the wood).

rewards.text: Lamp's thanks, cousin. The Pass House fires kept, and the carters with them. Warm hearth to you.

quests.title: Sit the Clamp
quests.summary: A charcoal clamp on the Upper hearths wants watching all night. Sit the first hour after midnight so the collier can sleep.

offer.say: #greet#. A charcoal clamp wants watching all night, or it breaks out and burns to ash. My mother kept these hearths, and hers before her, and neither ever lost a clamp. Sit the first hour after midnight by the clamps on the Upper hearths, and I'll sleep.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Not a crack in her. I'm late for everything else, but never for a clamp. Take two sacks of the good stuff. My grandmother would have said you'd make a collier, and she said that of nobody.

objectives.label: Sit by the clamps on the Upper hearths through the first hour after midnight, until one.
Bring two bundles of firewood to bank the clamp.

quests.title: Goats on the Scree
quests.summary: Mountain goats on the high lime quarry scree are kicking stones down on the kiln path. Bring one down and the rest will keep off.

offer.say: #greet#. Mountain goats on the quarry scree, kicking stones down on my kiln path. Bring one down and the rest'll keep off, #address#. And mind the road wolves that camp below the quarry. They're no friends of Frosthollow, eh.
offer.thanks: #thanks#. Solid work. The kiln path's clear, and the goats know it. You're not as soft as most from down the valley, #address#.

objectives.label: Bring down a mountain goat on the lime quarry scree.
Bring down a bandit of the camp below the quarry.

bonus.detail: brought down a bandit below the lime quarry
